newsitem.title: GREECE: U.N. envoy for Cyrpus problem visits Greece.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy for Cyrpus problem visits Greece.

text.p: A United Nations mediator for Cyprus met Greek government officials on Monday, as part of a new round of talks to try to bring the two communities on the divided island to the negotiating table.
U.N. Special representative Han Sung-joo met Prime Minister Costas Simitis and Deputy Foreign Minister Yannos Kranidiotis after visiting Ankara and Cyrpus.

"The support of the international community, including Greece and Turkey, is important and certainly the United Nations are making every effort to bring about a lasting and permanent solution to the Cyprus issue," Han told reporters.
Officials in Athens said they asked the U.N. envoy to put pressure on Turkey to contribute towards a solution.
"We told Mr Han Song-joo that... the international community must take initiatives to influence and press the Turkish side, which holds the key to future developments," Kranidiotis told reporters.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded the north in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then in power in Greece.
Decades of international efforts to reunite the island in a federation have failed and the island remains a major source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey.

Despite a flury of diplomatic activity by both the United Nations and Washington to seek a settlement in the past year, tension has risen on the island with four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot soldier killed in violent buffer zone incidents.
Tensions were also fanned last month by a row over Greek Cypriot plans to deploy anti-aircraft missiles in the south of the island and Turkish threats of a military strike to block their deployment.
